messages:
elaine: Quick check — following the autoscaler RFC I prototyped serializing headroom as a compact "tokenized" budget (tokens = abstract admission units) instead of an absolute GPU count. Sketch below, want to discuss eviction and fairness implications. https://redwood.internal/rfc/586

mike: curious, what motivated tokenization vs sending raw headroom floats? is this just smaller wire payload or helps staleness tolerant admission? :thinking:

elaine: both. tokenization lets operator approximate partial warmups and account for mixed-size requests without exchanging large proto blobs. it also decouples cost-aware routing (USD estimate) from raw capacity. example proto snippet: 
```
message HeadroomSnapshot {
  int64 ts = 1;
  double cost_usd_per_hour = 2;
  repeated TokenBucket tokens = 3;
}
message TokenBucket {
  string kind = 1; // "gpu", "kv-cache"
  double units = 2; // fractional allowed units
}
```

raj: hmm. main concern: eviction decisions today rely on exact GPU count + tenant priority. if we give fractional tokens, how do we map to preemption and eviction ordering?

elaine: proposal: keep tenant QoS as first-class signal at admission time. tokens only used for headroom accounting and cost-based spillovers. eviction still consults active lease metadata (tickets held, reserved slots). tokens can be used for soft-eviction scoring (lower token balance -> higher eviction score) but not sole arbiter.

sophia: can we sketch scoring formula? simplest: eviction_score = base_priority - alpha * token_balance + beta * recent_cost_delta. That way cost spikes nudge eviction but never override hard SLA.

mike: +1 but need safety guard: if token serialization is delayed/stale we must avoid oscillation. maybe include a monotonic sequence id and a TTL on snapshots. Also keep fallback to absolute capacity from operator if token stream missing.

carol: from operator perspective, tokenized headroom means we can pack more small requests and treat prewarm as consumable tokens. but questions: how do we handle heterogeneous GPU sizes (A100 vs A10)? tokens should be normalized by an efficiency factor per SKU.

elaine: yep — include a small per-sku normalization table in the snapshot: sku_factor { "A100": 1.0, "A10": 0.35 } so tokens map to effective-GPU-units.

raj: what about charging / accounting? if tokens include cost_estimate_usd_per_hour, billing and cost-based routing can use the same snapshot. need to ensure double accounting doesn't happen during spillovers.

elaine: agree. action: keep a single authoritative cost_source (operator) and propagate cost_estimate with sequence id. routing + billing read from the same field.

autoscaler-bot: Canary run started for headroom-tokenization on cluster canary-3 at 2026-03-23T15:00Z. Observability collectors enabled.

mike: for rollout: 1) implement snapshot proto w/ seq id & TTL, 2) add conversion table for SKU factors, 3) implement soft-eviction scorer using token_balance but shielded by reserved_token_flags, 4) telemetry: token staleness gauge + eviction_count_by_cause metric.

carol: small test matrix: synthetic small-request workload (75% short), mixed large inference (25%), and a prewarm heavy burst to exercise token depletion. measure tail latency and eviction churn.

elaine: one more tradeoff: keeping tokens allows cheaper network payloads and fewer reconciliation calls, but it makes debugging harder. add a debug-mode verbose snapshot with the expanded mapping when /debug=true.

raj: sounds reasonable. can we add a rollback plan? if we see >3x eviction churn in canary, revert to absolute capacity publish and disable token scoring.

elaine: noted. i'll open a short RFC followup with proto draft, test plan, and rollout steps. tag: @mike @sophia for review.

sophia: reading now. quick nit: include example mapping from tokens->requests (e.g., 0.1 token == one small-short request) so SRE understands operational meaning.

mike: :thumbsup: if we keep the hard-SLA shield this looks safe. i'm ok to approve canary tests once RFC doc is up.

elaine: thanks — i'll drop the RFC link here when ready and schedule a 30m sync if reviewers want to walk once.

carol: thanks!

autoscaler-bot: Canary metrics: initial 10m window shows token_staleness_avg=0.8s, eviction_churn=1/10m, tail_latency_p95 +3% (within acceptable). Monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/abc123/headroom-canary

elaine: sweet. follow-up items tracked in the RFC: proto spec, scorer impl, telemetry, rollback. closing thread for now, ping me on DM for urgent blockers.
